rows.jp: 微笑む少女の胸元に、自然な挙措で手が伸びた。
rows.en: With perfect naturalness, my hand reached for the smiling girl's chest.

ghs.en: With manners nonchalant my hand extended towards the chest of this smiling girl.
ghs.assessment: The hand naturally reaches toward the smiling girl's chest. The inverted modifier 'manners nonchalant' is ungrammatical literary affectation, and making the hand the sentence's agent does not require that inversion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My hand naturally reached toward the smiling girl's chest.'

highlights.text: With manners nonchalant my hand extended towards the chest of this smiling girl.

rows.jp: 隙を突かれたのか、美希は笑顔のまま身動き一つしなかった。
rows.en: Caught off guard, Miki remained utterly still, her smile frozen in place.

ghs.en: Perhaps because it caught her unaware, Miki didn't make one movement as she stood there smiling.

rows.en: Squish.

rows.jp: 気がつくと、俺はおっぱいを揉んでいた。
rows.en: By the time I came to my senses, I was squeezing her breast.

ghs.en: When I come to notice, I was rubbing breasts.
ghs.assessment: The source says that when he realized what he was doing, he was fondling her breasts. 'Come to notice' is unidiomatic, its tense clashes with 'was,' and the English drops the contextual possessor.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I came to, I was fondling her breasts.'

highlights.text: When I come to notice, I was rubbing breasts.

rows.jp: ほとんどないと思っていたその「板」には……薄いとはいえ確かな感触が。
rows.en: The ‘plank’ I had assumed almost nonexistent possessed—thin though it was—an unmistakable softness.

ghs.en: I flatly thought that there would be about nothing on this Chopping Board... but, weak as it may be, there is certainly that tactile sensation.

rows.en: ‘...Oops.’

rows.jp: 笑顔のまま、口元を引きつらせる。
rows.en: Her smile remained in place while the corners of her mouth twitched.

ghs.en: Still smiling, the edge of her lips begin to twitch.
ghs.assessment: The mouth remains smiling but starts to twitch. The English has a subject-verb disagreement and replaces the natural mouth or corners-of-the-mouth expression with the singular 'edge of her lips.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Still smiling, the corners of her mouth began to twitch.'

highlights.text: the edge of her lips begin to twitch

rows.en: ‘Sorry. I wasn't thinking, and my hand...’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sorry, alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own."

rows.jp: 「いえ、うっかりしていたわたしが悪いのです」
rows.en: ‘No. The fault is mine for letting my guard down.’

ghs.en: Miki: "No, it's my bad for having been careless."

rows.jp: 「あの、こんなこと俺が言うのもなんだけど……ちょっと膨らんでるね。良かったね！」
rows.en: ‘I know I'm hardly in a position to say this, but... you've developed a little. Congratulations!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uhm, I shouldn't exactly be saying this but... they've bulged out a bit. That's great!"
ghs.assessment: He awkwardly congratulates her on having filled out a little. 'Bulged out' suggests an abrupt protrusion or swelling rather than modest physical development, making the line harsher and less idiomatic than the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'you've filled out a little.'

rows.jp: 「恐縮です。いつ手を離していただけますでしょうか」
rows.en: ‘You are too kind. Might I ask when you intend to remove your hand?’

ghs.en: Miki: "Much obliged. When will this hand finally distance itself?"
ghs.assessment: Her mock-politeness asks when he will kindly remove his hand. The English makes the hand an autonomous subject, uses the unidiomatic reflexive 'distance itself,' and loses the pointedly courteous request directed at him.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Much obliged. And when might you remove your hand?'

highlights.text: When will this hand finally distance itself

rows.en: ‘There's hope for your future after all.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "We've finally got some hope for the future here."

rows.jp: 「うーん、喜べばいいのか怒ればいいのか。で、いつまで触っておられるつもりでしょうか？」
rows.en: ‘Hmm. I can't decide whether to be pleased or angry. Also, how long do you intend to keep touching me?’

ghs.en: Miki: "Hmmm, should I be happy, should I be angry? Well, for how long do you intend to continue touching this?"

rows.jp: 「俺は感慨深いよ。あの小さかった、いやさ、平べったかった美希が三次元的立体感を手に入れるなんて」
rows.en: ‘It moves me, honestly. Little Miki—no, flat Miki—has finally acquired three-dimensional volume.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm deeply moved here. For the so tiny, nay, so tabular Miki has obtained the solid feeling of tridimensionality!"
ghs.assessment: The mock-grand statement says that formerly tiny—or rather flat—Miki has acquired three-dimensional volume. The English is syntactically broken after 'For,' and 'tabular' and 'solid feeling of tridimensionality' are technical malapropisms rather than controlled grandiosity.
ghs.remedy: Use 'To think little—no, flat—Miki has finally acquired three-dimensional volume!'

highlights.text: For the so tiny, nay, so tabular Miki has obtained the solid feeling of tridimensionality

rows.en: ‘Miki?’

rows.jp: もみもみする手を止めて、顔を見る。
rows.en: I stopped kneading and looked at her face.

ghs.en: I stop the hand going all rubby rubby and look at her face.

rows.en: Miki was crying.
‘W-Wait.’
Did I make her cry?
Did I make her cry?
Silent tears.

rows.jp: 嗚咽もなく、頬の曲線を滑りおちる。
rows.en: No sobs. They simply traced the curves of her cheeks.

ghs.en: with sobbing neither, simply slipping down the curve of her cheeks.
ghs.assessment: The tears slide down the curve of her cheeks without a sob. 'With sobbing neither' is not grammatical English and obscures the clean continuation from the preceding fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'without a sob, simply slipping down the curve of her cheeks.'

rows.jp: 芸術家が美しさに胸打たれて流す涙があるとすれば、これだろう。
rows.en: If beauty could ever move an artist to tears, those tears would look like this.

ghs.en: If I were to imagine the tears flowing from an artist whose heart has been struck by beauty, this would be it.

rows.jp: セクハラされて流すものではない、はず。
rows.en: They were not the tears of someone being harassed. Probably.

ghs.en: This is not the shedding of someone subjected to sexual harassment, it can't be.

rows.en: I did not know what to do.
So I stopped.
Because I did not understand.

ghs.assessment: The source gives his inability to understand as the reason he stops. The impersonal 'there's no understanding' replaces that experiencer with an abstract absence and is unnatural in context.
ghs.remedy: Use 'because I don't understand.'

rows.jp: やがて美希はぐっと涙をぬぐった。
rows.en: At last, Miki scrubbed the tears away.

ghs.en: Before long Miki well and wiped off her tears,
ghs.assessment: Miki soon wipes her tears away firmly. The stray 'well and' makes the sentence ungrammatical and does not convey the decisive force of the adverb.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Before long, Miki firmly wiped away her tears.'

highlights.text: Before long Miki well and wiped off her tears

rows.jp: まぶたの上を腕が往復して、出てきたのはいつもの笑顔。
rows.en: Her arm swept back and forth across her eyelids. When it lowered, her usual smile had returned.

ghs.en: her forearms making a trip around and over her eyelids, and what came out behind them was her smile of always.
ghs.assessment: Her arm passes back and forth over her eyelids, revealing her usual smile. The English changes one arm into plural forearms, invents a trip 'around' the eyelids, and ends with the calque 'smile of always.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her arm passed back and forth over her eyes, and out came her usual smile.'

highlights.text: her forearms making a trip around and over her eyelids, and what came out behind them was her smile of always

rows.en: ‘Ehehe.’
‘All right! Back to cleaning!’

ghs.assessment: She cheerfully turns back to cleaning. 'To cleaning' is not an English idiom for resuming a task and makes the energetic repetition sound malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use 'All right—back to cleaning, cleaning!'

rows.en: ‘But first... Hah!’
‘Gwohhh!’

rows.jp: 腕の秘孔（二の腕の中ほどあたり）を一本拳で突かれた。
rows.en: She drove one knuckle into a secret pressure point halfway up my upper arm.

ghs.en: My arm's pressure point (around the center of the forearm) was struck with the exact knuckletip of a fist.
ghs.assessment: The parenthetical locates the point around the middle of the upper arm, not the forearm. That anatomical change makes the explicit gloss factually wrong.
ghs.remedy: Use 'around the middle of my upper arm.'

rows.jp: 「いたた、筋がすごくいたいよー！　握り拳をぎゅっと作るとピキーンって痛むよー！」
rows.en: ‘Ow! The tendon really hurts! Every time I make a fist, it goes PING and shoots pain through my arm!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "OwChCh, muscle reeeally hurts! When I clench my fist tight it hurts like an electric shooock!"

rows.en: I writhed in agony.

ghs.assessment: The source is a compact fragment describing him writhing in agony. The translation adds an inverted finite construction that is neither ordinary narration nor controlled comic diction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I writhed in agony,' or retain the fragment as 'Me, writhing in agony.'

rows.en: ‘Swish, swish♪’
Miki cleaned.

ghs.assessment: The fragment simply shows Miki cleaning. The subject-verb inversion is unidiomatic and adds an affected cadence absent from the plain source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miki went on sweeping.'

rows.en: And then—
‘...You are Miki, right?’
‘Huh?’
‘No. Sorry.’

ghs.assessment: He says 'No, sorry.' The English replaces the apology with a dismissal that nothing is wrong, changing both the speech act and his stance.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No—sorry.'

rows.jp: 「それは胸があったから美希ではないという意味のご発言でございましょうか？」
rows.en: ‘Was that your way of saying that having breasts disqualifies me from being Miki?’

ghs.en: Miki: "Would that utterance be to the meaning that if I have presence of breasts then I cannot be Miki?"
ghs.assessment: Her deliberately formal question asks whether he means she cannot be Miki because she has breasts. 'Be to the meaning' and 'have presence of breasts' are ungrammatical pseudo-formality rather than natural ceremonious English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Am I to understand that, because I have breasts, I cannot possibly be Miki?'

highlights.text: Would that utterance be to the meaning that if I have presence of breasts then I cannot be Miki

rows.jp: ぺっ、と架空のツバを吐く。
rows.en: She spat an imaginary glob at me.

ghs.assessment: The present-tense narration has him mime spitting with an imaginary gob. The adverb 'Imaginarily' is malformed in this use, its capitalization is erroneous, and the translation switches tense.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Pah. I mimed spitting.'

rows.en: ‘Honestly, I'm disappointed.’
‘Gasp.’

rows.jp: 「何人の固定ファンを手放したか」
rows.en: ‘Think how many loyal fans you've just lost.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "How many fixated fans did you just lose?"
ghs.assessment: 固定ファン means established, loyal, or dedicated fans. 'Fixated fans' instead describes people obsessively attached and changes a marketing-style category into a psychological judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'How many dedicated fans do you think you just lost?'

rows.en: ‘Loyal fans?’

ghs.assessment: The repeated term refers to loyal or dedicated fans, not fans who are fixated. The error is repeated here as dialogue terminology.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Dedicated fans?'

rows.jp: 「たとえロリっ娘でなくとも胸がないことで、幼稚園児をその聖域とする社会不適合者の支持を受けることも不可能ではないのに……」
rows.en: ‘Even if you aren't a little girl, having no breasts whatsoever could still win you the support of social rejects whose sacred ideal is the kindergarten set...’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because it's not impossible you've been receiving the endorsement of those societally nonconforming people who make the kindergarten into their Holy Ground due to your having a flat chest, even if you aren't exactly loli..."
ghs.assessment: The source describes social misfits who treat kindergarten-aged children as their sacred domain. The English changes the children, 幼稚園児, into the institution 'the kindergarten,' materially altering the target of the grotesque joke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'who regard kindergarteners as their sacred domain.'

highlights.text: make the kindergarten into their Holy Ground

rows.en: ‘The world is doomed.’

ghs.en: Miki: "It's just the end of the world here!"

rows.jp: 「美希のばかっ、セクハラしちゃってごめんよ！」
rows.en: ‘You idiot, Miki! And I'm sorry I groped you!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Miki you dummy, sorry for sexually harassing you!"

rows.jp: 罵声と謝罪を同時にこなして、俺は走り去る。
rows.en: Having delivered an insult and an apology in the same breath, I ran away.

ghs.en: Managing simultaneous words of scorn and of apology, I run away.
